title: Development of Amelogenin-chitosan Hydrogel for In Vitro Enamel Regrowth with a Dense Interface
protocol: Select a human third molar without any restored caries.
Remove the root portion of the molar.
Cut the crown of the molar longitudinally into slices 2 mm thick using a water-cooled low-speed diamond saw.
Ultrasonically clean these slices for 2 min.
Rinse the cleaned slices with deionized water 3 times.
Etch the tooth slices with 30% phosphoric acid for 30 sec.
Immediately rinse the etched slices with deionized water after acid treatment.
Ultrasonically clean the etched slices for 2 min.
Rinse the ultrasonically cleaned slices with deionized water 3 times.
Dissolve 1% (w/v) chitosan in a 1% (v/v) acetic acid solution followed by stirring at 80 °C O/N.
Cool the chitosan solution to RT after overnight stirring.
Filter the cooled chitosan solution using a 0.45 μm filter.
Adjust the pH value of the filtered chitosan solution to 5.0 by adding 1 M NaOH solution.
Weigh out calcium chloride (CaCl2) and prepare a 0.1 M solution.
Mix the calcium chloride solution until it is clear using a vortex.
Adjust the pH value of the calcium chloride solution to 11 by adding 1 M NaOH solution.
Weigh out dibasic sodium phosphate and prepare a 0.1 M solution.
Vortex the solution until clear.
Add 20 g of LB Agar powder into 500 ml deionized water.
Autoclave the solution at 121 °C for 20 min.
Let agar cool to ~ 55 °C.
Add ampicillin (100 μg/ml) into agar solution.
Transfer the agar solution to Petri dishes.
Cool each plate until solid, then flip plates to avoid condensation on the agar.
Store plates in plastic bags at 4 °C.
Streak the LB agar plate with recombinant cells from glycerol stock (-80 °C).
Incubate the plates overnight at 37 °C.
Prepare 50 ml of NZCYM media and autoclave the media at 121 °C for 30 min.
Allow the media to cool down, then add 50 µl of 100 µg/ml ampicillin to the 50 ml media.
Inoculate a single colony from the LB agar plate into the 50ml NZCYM media supplemented with ampicillin.
Incubate the cells overnight in a shaking incubator at 37 °C.
Prepare 1 L of NZCYM media and autoclave the media at 121 °C for 30 min.
Add 1 ml of 100 mg/ml ampicillin to 1,000 ml media.
Take an optical density (OD) reading as a blank using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Inoculate 10 ml of cell culture into 1,000 ml media.
Read the optical density at 595 nm immediately after inoculation.
Take periodic optical density readings to track growth.
Induce bacterial growth with 700 µl IPTG when OD reaches 0.75~0.8.
Harvest cells when OD reaches 1.1.
Pour flask contents into 6 plastic bottles and balance them.
Centrifuge for 20 min at 8,554 x g at 4 °C.
Store the cell pellet in -20 °C overnight.
Combine cell pellets from all tubes in a 50 ml tube.
Add 3.5 ml of 4M Guanidine HCl per liter of fermentation.
Sonicate on ice for 30 sec, twice with one-minute intervals.
Dilute cell volume six times with 0.5% formic acid and stir for 2 hours in a cold room.
Centrifuge for 30 min at 8,554 x g at 4 °C.
Keep the supernatant after centrifugation.
Add 20% saturated ammonium sulfate to the supernatant and stir overnight in a cold room.
Centrifuge again for 30 min at 8,554 x g at 4 °C.
Keep the pellet from this step.
Reconstitute pellets with 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA).
Load onto a C4 column (10 x 250 mm, 5 µm).
Fractionate using a linear gradient of A=0.1% TFA and B=60% acetonitrile in TFA at 1.5 ml·min-1.
Freeze the protein solution on dry ice.
Lyophilize the frozen sample overnight.
Add 200 µg of rp172 into a tube containing 960 µl of 1% chitosan solution, then mix using a vortex until the solution is clear.
Add 25 µl of 0.1 M CaCl2 solution to the amelogenin-containing chitosan solution, followed by mixing with a vortex.
Add 15 µl of 0.1 M Na2HPO4 solution to the amelogenin-containing chitosan solution and mix with a vortex for 5 min.
Adjust the pH of the CS-AMEL solution to 6.5 by carefully adding 1 M NaOH solution.

Dissolve magnesium chloride (MgCl2, 0.2 mM), calcium chloride (CaCl2, 1 mM), potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KH2PO4, 4 mM), potassium chloride (KCl, 16 mM) and ammonium chloride (NH4Cl, 4.5 mM) in 20 mM HEPES buffer.
Adjust the pH of the artificial saliva solution to 7.0 with 1 M NaOH.
Store the artificial saliva solution at 4 °C before use.
Add sodium fluoride (NaF, 300 ppm) to the artificial saliva solution prior to use.
Apply about 20 µl CS-AMEL hydrogel to the etched tooth slice using a syringe.
Dry the hydrogel-covered tooth slice in a desiccator at room temperature for 2 hours.
Transfer the tooth slice to a beaker containing 30 ml of artificial saliva solution.
Cover the beaker with aluminum foil and keep it in an oven at 37 °C for 7 days.
Remove the tooth slice from the beaker after 7 days.
Dry the tooth slice in a desiccator at room temperature.
Load the sample into a FIB-SEM instrument.
Finish all alignments according to the operating instructions.
Perform fine Z adjustment at least twice.
Deposit a carbon layer (15 × 3 µm) on the sample.
Mill the sample carefully at the upper, lower and right sides of the carbon layer.
Cut the bottom side of the thin piece after milling.
Check ion beam alignment before each milling step.
Weld a Pt tip on the thin piece.
Cut the left side to separate the sample piece.
Check ion beam alignment before the welding step.
Lift out the Pt tip with the sample slowly.
Mount the lamellar sample onto a lift-out TEM grid.
Detach the tip from the sample.
Thin the sample until its thickness is less than 100 nm.
Remove the sample from the instrument.
Perform TEM observation.
Keep the repaired tooth slice in an ultrasonic cleaner (42 kHz, 100 W) for 10 minutes.
Observe the interface between the repaired layer and natural enamel with a backscattered-electron SEM analysis.
Measure hardness at 20 test points on each repaired enamel surface using a nano-indenter with a Berkovich tip.
Measure elastic modulus at 20 test points on each repaired enamel surface using a nano-indenter with a Berkovich tip.
Wash the tooth slice with Tris buffer saline (TBS) for 15 minutes.
Block the tooth slice with 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in TBS for 15 minutes.
Incubate the sample overnight with primary antibody (Chicken Anti-Amelogenin, 1:500 dilution in TBS containing 0.1% BSA and 0.3% Triton X-100).
Wash the sample with TBS for 30 minutes.
Incubate the sample overnight with secondary antibody (Anti-chicken FITC, 1:100 dilution in TBS).
Wash the sample with TBS for 30 minutes.
Leave the sample to dry for another 30 minutes.
Observe the sample by fluorescence microscopy.
